The Bihar Discoms have objected that the claim of the Petitioner is barred by the principles contained in Order II Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC). As per Order II Rule 2(2) of the CPC, if a party omits to sue in respect of any portion of his claim, the said party cannot afterwards sue in respect of the portion so omitted and as per Order II Rule 2(3) of the CPC, if a party omits to claims a relief arising out of a cause of action, the said party will be barred from claiming such relief subsequently in a separate suit. Thus, having omitted to claim carrying cost, which is part of the Change in Law claims and arises out of the same cause of action, in Petition No.470/MP/2019, the Petitioner is barred from filing the present Petition seeking carrying cost for the said Change in Law events under Order II Rule 2 of the CPC. The purpose behind Order II Rule 2 of the CPC, as elucidated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Coffee Board v. Ramesh Exports (P) Limited, [(2014) 6 SCC 424], is to ensure that no party is vexed twice for the same cause of action. APTEL in its judgment dated 25.10.2018 in Appeal No. 185 of 2015 in the case of Kalani Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. Rajasthan Electricity Regulatory Commission and Ors.
